summary.text: Organic reactions are chemical reactions that involve organic compounds.
They are used to build new organic molecules, and drugs, plastics, food additives and fabrics depend on them.
Most of them are polar reactions, where electron pairs move from a clear source to a clear sink.

facts.label: Oldest reactions
facts.value: Burning organic fuels and turning fats into soap

facts.label: Modern start
facts.value: Modern organic chemistry starts with the Wöhler synthesis in 1828

facts.label: Largest class
facts.value: Polar reactions make up the vast majority

items.prompt: A chemist watches pairs of electrons move from a clear electron-rich spot to a clear electron-poor spot, and atoms change charge on the way. Which mechanistic class is this?

options.label: A radical reaction
A pericyclic reaction
A polar reaction
A redox reaction

items.explain: Polar reactions move electron pairs from a defined source to a defined sink, and the atoms involved change charge.

items.prompt: In another reaction, the key players carry single unpaired electrons that move one at a time. Which mechanistic class fits?

options.label: A polar reaction
A radical reaction
A pericyclic reaction
A redox reaction

items.explain: Radical reactions involve species with unpaired electrons and the movement of single electrons.

items.prompt: A student says that a list of the starting chemicals is enough to tell you every step of how a reaction happens. What is wrong with that?

options.label: The mechanism always has exactly three steps
Only the products can reveal the mechanism
A mechanism can never be worked out at all
The list alone does not always make the stepwise mechanism clear

items.explain: Each reaction has a stepwise mechanism, but those steps are not always clear from a list of reactants alone.

items.prompt: A reaction starts as a substitution, but it goes by first adding a group and then removing one. What does this show about sorting reactions?

options.label: Some reactions fit more than one category
Substitutions are really a type of redox
Each reaction must be filed under one type
Addition and elimination cannot happen together

items.explain: Some reactions fit into more than one category, for example substitution reactions that follow an addition-elimination pathway.

items.prompt: A reaction named after four inventors is a mouthful to say, so chemists write it as the CBS reduction. What is this an example of?

options.label: Naming a reaction after its reagent type
Naming a reaction after its mechanism
Shortening a long named reaction to an abbreviation
Replacing a name with its Nobel Prize year

items.explain: When a named reaction is difficult to pronounce or very long, it helps to use an abbreviation.

items.prompt: In one kind of reaction, water is consumed. What is the name for the opposite of a reaction that splits water off as two reactants combine?

options.label: Condensation
Hydrolysis
Polymerization
Saponification

items.explain: In condensation reactions a small molecule, usually water, is split off; the opposite, where water is consumed, is hydrolysis.
